story.title: Dennis Haskins, known for his role in Saved by the Bell, passes away at 75
story.summary: Dennis Haskins, famous for portraying Principal Richard Belding on the sitcom 'Saved by the Bell,' has died at the age of 75. His agent confirmed the news, but the cause of death has not been disclosed.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Haskins' death resonate with viewers?
explore_lenses.title: A role that spanned the franchise
explore_lenses.summary: Haskins was more than a one-series supporting player: Principal Richard Belding connected the Disney-originated show to NBC's long-running teen sitcom and its follow-up. That continuity made the character a familiar authority figure for multiple audiences.

claims.text: Haskins played Belding first on Disney Channel's "Good Morning, Miss Bliss," then throughout NBC's "Saved by the Bell" from 1989 to 1993, and later on "Saved by the Bell: The New Class" from 1993 to 2000.

He returned to the role in a 2015 "Tonight Show" sketch with Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Elizabeth Berkley, Mario Lopez and Tiffani Thiessen, showing the character's continued association with the original cast.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about his death and health?
explore_lenses.title: Death confirmed; cause remains undisclosed
explore_lenses.summary: His agent confirmed Haskins' death, but no official cause or further details had been released in the initial reporting. A longtime caretaker separately described a private history of Parkinson's disease and other health problems; that does not establish a cause of death.

claims.text: Agent Jay Schachter confirmed Haskins' death; the Associated Press reported that additional details were not immediately available.
ABC News reported that Haskins' cause of death had not been released.

Kimberly Snow, identified by the Los Angeles Times as Haskins' friend and longtime caretaker, said he had quietly battled Parkinson's disease and other health issues and died in a Burbank assisted-living facility; this account has not been presented as an official cause-of-death determination.

explore_lenses.title: Former cast members emphasize kindness
explore_lenses.summary: Early remembrances focus on Haskins' relationships with colleagues and fans rather than new production or memorial plans. Schachter and former co-star Tiffani Thiessen each described him as personally generous.

claims.text: Schachter, Haskins' agent for more than 20 years, called the death a "tragic loss" and said Haskins loved his fans and made time for them.
Thiessen said Haskins had been a steady presence in her teenage years and recalled his kindness and the cast's shared memories; AP also reported that Lark Voorhies posted that she was heartbroken.

story_report.summary: Dennis Haskins, the actor best known as Principal Richard Belding in the “Saved by the Bell” franchise, has died at 75, his agent Jay Schachter confirmed. Haskins’ portrayal of the school principal spanned multiple series and remained closely associated with the original cast in later appearances. No official cause of death has been released, and public reporting reviewed did not identify funeral or memorial arrangements.

sections.heading: Dennis Haskins’ Principal Belding Legacy
sections.body: Haskins first played Richard Belding on Disney Channel’s “Good Morning, Miss Bliss,” before taking the role to NBC’s “Saved by the Bell” from 1989 to 1993. He continued as Belding on “Saved by the Bell: The New Class” through 2000. In 2015, he revisited the character in a “Tonight Show” sketch alongside Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Elizabeth Berkley, Mario Lopez and Tiffani Thiessen.

sections.heading: Dennis Haskins Remembered by Colleagues
sections.body: Schachter, who had represented Haskins for more than 20 years, called his death a “tragic loss” and said the actor loved his fans and made time for them. Thiessen described Haskins as a steady presence during her teenage years and recalled his kindness and the cast’s shared memories. Lark Voorhies also said she was heartbroken, according to the Associated Press.

unresolved.text: No official memorial, funeral or estate announcement was identified in the reporting reviewed.

related_stories.title: Tu-95 Bomber Crash in Far East Claims Six Lives
related_stories.summary: A Russian Tu-95 bomber crashed during a training flight in the Amur region, resulting in the deaths of six crew members. The incident occurred shortly after takeoff from the Ukrainka air base, which had been used to shelter aircraft following significant damage from Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb in June 2025.
